about: How an agent's question (AskUserQuestion) ended, read back from the result text the engine wrote
for the agent: one set of cases both clients are proved against. `@orbit/shared`'s
the web renders) against this file; OrbitKit's `QuestionRecordsTests` reads the same file.
`outcome`: the questions as the call's input carries them, the result's text and whether it was an
error → `{kind: answered, answers}` (one entry per question: the picked options' indices, ascending,
and the words typed; null where the result names none), `{kind: replied, words}` (Chat about this),
or null (no result, a failure, a wording the reader does not know: the card shows the result itself).
`lead`: a question's opening on the folded card: every run of whitespace one space, trimmed.
`lines`: what the folded card writes under the openings. For `answered`, one per question: the picked
options' labels in the order offered, then the typed words in “”, joined by " · " (U+00B7 between
two spaces); null where there is no answer. For `replied`, the reply in “”. None when the outcome is null.

questions.question: On iPad, what should a swipe right from the left edge do? Today there are two places on the iPad where the swipe does nothing: (1) the hidden sidebar only opens from the toolbar button; (2) the in-column pages with a Back button (a folder's page, a project's sessions page, a task opened over its project, a runner's engine or name page) only go back from that button. On the iPhone the same swipe opens the drawer on a list page and goes back on a pushed page.

options.label: Both, like the iPhone (Recommended)
options.description: On a list page, swiping right from the screen's left edge opens the sidebar (swiping left on it closes it). On an in-column page with a Back button, swiping right from that column's left edge goes back one page.

options.label: Open the sidebar only
options.description: Swiping right from the screen's left edge opens the sidebar; going back still uses only the Back button.

options.label: Swipe back only
options.description: On an in-column page with a Back button, swiping right goes back; the sidebar still opens only from the toolbar button.
